title: Do you not yet understand (Mark 8:1–21)
hookLine: another feeding, and the disciples still worry about bread

lines: FOUR THOUSAND, THREE DAYS, NO FOOD.
cards: A crowd of about four thousand has been with Jesus for three days, and they're out of food. The disciples ask where anyone could find bread out here. There are seven loaves and a few small fish.
He gives thanks, breaks, and they hand it out. Everyone eats, and seven baskets of scraps are left over. Then they get into a boat, and somebody realizes they've forgotten to bring bread.
One loaf. And the worrying starts again, as if they'd never seen it work out.

teach.h: A SECOND FEEDING, IN GENTILE COUNTRY.
teach.b: First, the second feeding. Mark has told this before: five thousand, five loaves. Now it happens again, with four thousand.
Why twice? Many readers notice where it happens: in the Decapolis, the Gentile country Jesus was just walking through. The first crowd was mostly Jewish; this one may not be.
Bread for the children, then bread past the edge of the table, right after the mother's crumbs. Second, the leaven.

teach.h: BEWARE THE LEAVEN. WE FORGOT BREAD.
teach.b: In the boat Jesus warns them: beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod. Mark doesn't say what the leaven is.
Luke's Gospel calls it hypocrisy; many readers hear something small that spreads unseen, the way yeast works through dough. And the disciples hear only one word: bread. We forgot the bread.
Third, his questions, one after another, in the Douay-Rheims: "Having eyes, see you not? and having ears, hear you not? neither do you remember." Then he makes them count.
The five loaves among five thousand: how many baskets left?
Twelve, they say. The seven among four thousand? Seven.

teach.h: HOW DO YOU NOT YET UNDERSTAND?
teach.b: And he says: "How do you not yet understand?" Mark ends the scene there, with the question hanging. Fourth, the baskets.
Mark even uses two different Greek words for them, one for each feeding, as if each basket was its own memory. The disciples aren't stupid. They're simply human: the fear is louder than the memory.
Jesus doesn't answer their fear with a new miracle. He asks them to count the old ones.

how: Many Catholics keep a habit of recalling God's past gifts, often in the evening examen or in thanksgiving after Communion, and preachers often pair Mark's two feedings with the Eucharist.

o: the flat, unrisen bread eaten at Passover
something small and hidden that spreads unseen
a loaf of bread blessed for a holy meal

games.q: count the baskets — tap the pairs.

s: Mark tells the feeding of a crowd only once
he tells it twice: five thousand with five loaves, then four thousand with seven.
when Jesus warns about leaven, the disciples think he means bread
they hear "bread" and worry that they forgot to bring some.
Jesus answers their worry with a new miracle in the boat
he asks them to remember and count the baskets from before.

games.q: you're in the boat with one loaf for thirteen people. Jesus warns you about leaven. what goes through your head?
o: he must mean something bigger than bread.
we should turn the boat around.
games.why: they reason among themselves that they have no bread. and he asks, "How do you not yet understand?"

practice: Go back to a time you didn't know how it would work out, and it did: money that came through, a friend who showed up, a door that opened when you'd run out of doors.

Picture it in detail, where you were and who was there, and count it like a basket; if there's another, count that too. If you pray, simply say thank you for it; if you don't, let the memory sit next to today's worry.

wordCard.voice: Leaven. The small hidden thing Jesus warns about in the boat, of the Pharisees and of Herod, that spreads unseen through dough. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: do you not yet understand? the last line of the scene, left hanging.

carryVoice: Your line: remember the baskets. Fear talks loud, and the baskets are still there to count. Day two hundred twelve, done.

sources.q: Having eyes, see you not? and having ears, hear you not? neither do you remember.
How do you not yet understand?
